conviction_note: abs_move 16 from the 16.6% option-implied move and an 11% median / 26.5% last reaction, not shrunk for sign. p_up 55 is a mild lean: the company said on Oct 16 that US demand is rising, the adult Ultomiris TA-TMA trial failed in-quarter, the J-code covered the full quarter, and 17.7% of shares are short with short interest rising into the print and the skew paying for upside. Against that, the Q3 revenue bar is disputed ($30.9M to $38.0M) and the FY consensus of $127.5M implies a steep H2 ramp that a lumpy rare-disease launch could miss. Because the lean agrees with the skew it is partly priced, so p_up stays near 50. The findings sum to +2.8 against a scaled +1.6; the gap comes from several small, partly priced positives counted on their own, while the scaled number carries the bar risk through p_up.

positioning_check: Short interest 12,833,757 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up 1,404,990 from 10-15 (11,428,767), about 17.7% of shares outstanding, 9.6 days to cover; 9-30 was 11.38M / 6.95 DTC (https://equibles.com/stocks/omer/shortinterest, read 2026-11-16). findings.finding: In its Oct 16, 2026 release on the negative CHMP re-examination, Omeros said it is ending the EU YARTEMLEA compassionate-use program 'because U.S. commercial demand for drug supply is rising'. This is a company-level statement, made two weeks after Q3 closed, that US demand in and after Q3 was growing; the Q2 net-sales baseline is $28.5M against a disputed Q3 bar of $31-38M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue is the line this stock trades on: the Q2 2026 print ($28.5M against about $12.7M expected, +188% q/q) closed +26.55%; the Q1 2026 first launch quarter ($9.9M) closed -7.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sentence sat inside an EU-rejection release and the stock fell 12-15% that day on the CHMP headline (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/omeros-shares-slide-after-chmp-upholds-negative-opinion-on-drug-analyst-sees-buying-opportunity-at-16/cZxKQ9ERBtG). Had the demand line been priced, the stock would have recovered toward the late-September level of about $20-21, but it sits at $17.09 and short interest rose 1.4M shares after the release.
findings.independence: Same document as nothing else filed here. Qualitatively corroborated by the Q2 call (ordering frequency 'increased meaningfully', accounts 30 to 73), https://www.webull.com/news/15432272178070528. That source is older, but it is a different document.

findings.finding: AstraZeneca/Alexion's adult/adolescent Phase 3 of Ultomiris in HSCT-TMA (n=146) missed its primary endpoint, event-free survival at 26 weeks against placebo, on 2026-07-27, inside Q3. This removes the only late-stage adult competitor for YARTEMLEA's main (about 75% adult) market and may support Q3 ordering and the outlook narrative; the pediatric trial was positive and AZ is preparing pediatric filings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OMER gapped up on 2026-07-27 on this readout (MarketBeat 'shares gap up' alert of that date); no earnings-day history on a competitor line.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock gapped up the day of the readout. What is left is whether management quantifies any competitive effect on the call (e.g., off-label eculizumab displacement). If that were priced, the call commentary would be expected to add nothing, and the remaining value is small.
findings.independence: Counterparty-sourced (AZ). The 'residual off-label eculizumab use' watch item is in the finviz preview, https://finviz.com/news/421146/omeros-faces-its-first-real-test-of-whether-the-yartemlia-launch-can-keep-climbing

findings.finding: Reimbursement stepped up through the window: the permanent YARTEMLEA J-code took effect July 1, 2026, so Q3 is the first full quarter under it; CMS's NTAP of up to $287k per course (about 65% cap, covering the about 30% Medicare share of allo-transplant patients) took effect Oct 1, 2026, so it should show in Q4 outlook commentary on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a reimbursement line; the J-code and NTAP were announced in July, around the Q2 print that rose +26.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since July, so the level is priced. The unpriced part is the first quantification of how the NTAP is changing Q4 ordering, which nobody has seen. If that were priced, the FY consensus would sit at the top of its $103-151M range rather than the middle.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 call document with the corroboration cited in finding 1. The finviz preview independently flags NTAP as an outlook item: https://finviz.com/news/421146/omeros-faces-its-first-real-test-of-whether-the-yartemlia-launch-can-keep-climbing

findings.finding: The bar is high and disputed. The FY2026 revenue consensus of $127.5M (3 analysts, range $103-151M) against $38.4M reported in H1 implies about $89M in H2, and Q3 estimates of $36-38M (Benzinga, Chartmill) require +26-33% q/q from $28.5M. Management gave no guidance, distributor inventory was a steady 1.5 weeks, and a single preview carries $30.9M. A lumpy rare-disease launch with no Q3 data points could print in the low $30Ms and read as a miss against the higher numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First launch quarter Q1 2026 ($9.9M) -7.65%; Q2 2026 big beat +26.55%. The name moves hard in both directions on the revenue line.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimate dispersion ($30.9M vs $38.0M) means part of the street is anchored above what a merely steady ramp delivers. If priced, the stock would have reset lower and estimates would converge; instead the 3-analyst average target is $27.50. Capped small because the bar itself is unsourced to a guide.
findings.independence: Bar dispersion corroborated by https://finviz.com/news/421146/omeros-faces-its-first-real-test-of-whether-the-yartemlia-launch-can-keep-climbing ($30.9M) and https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OMER/earnings-forecasts ($36.0M). Crowded short and upside skew argue against sizing this larger.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q says $100.0M of the Novo zaltenibart milestones is one-time and 'achievable in the near term', which is about 8% of the roughly $1.2B market cap. As of today ClinicalTrials.gov lists no Novo-sponsored zaltenibart trial (only Omeros' completed Phase 1/2), so a Phase-3-start trigger looks not yet hit. An announcement or timing update on this call would be a positive surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings-day history; the Oct 2025 deal announcement was the last Novo-related move.
findings.why_not_priced: Triggers and timing are undisclosed and no trial is registered, so the market cannot date it. If it were priced, an 8-K would have been filed, or analyst targets would cluster on a dated cash event. The low probability of an announcement in this window keeps the central size small.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: short interest rose 1.4M shares (+12%) to 12.83M (about 17.7% of shares out, 9.6 days to cover) between the Oct 15 and Oct 30 settlements, i.e., shorts added after the CHMP rejection. Meanwhile the option skew is -11.5 vol points (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.25.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print with short interest near 17% of float gave +26.55%; the Q4 2025 print +14.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is a published series, but its asymmetry is the mechanism: a merely in-line revenue print forces covering at 9.6 DTC. If priced, short interest would be falling into the print, as it did into September, not rising.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -11.51 and P/C OI 0.25 (sealed baseline file). Also https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/omer/short-interest (older settlements).

findings.finding: Insiders sold steadily after the Q2 pop: CAO David Borges sold 10,000 at $20.95 on 2026-09-23 under 10b5-1 and reportedly held no shares afterward; VP Peter Cancelmo sold 25,000 at $18.54 on Aug 31; director Thomas Cable sold 15,000 at $18.45 in late August. findings.why_not_priced: Small sales, partly planned, public via Form 4. If they were informative, the stock would have weakened on them rather than holding near $20 into late September. Shrunk for the crowded short.
